(Approved carrier — ITV News; facts cross-referenced across multiple approved outlets; snippet-sourced, direct fetch timed out)
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood's Immigration and Asylum Bill would double the wait for indefinite leave to remain (ILR) from five to ten years, and up to 20 years for refugees, applied retrospectively to people already in the UK.
Almost 80 Labour MPs signed a private letter urging Andy Burnham to pause/dilute the reforms, warning he risked "losing progressive voters"; the MPs wrote that with a "10-20 year settlement period, the UK would be an international outlier," and that the change would hit NHS nurses and care staff already living in the UK.
Former deputy prime minister Angela Rayner said the changes to indefinite leave to remain for people already living in the UK would be a "breach of trust".
At the bill's second reading (Monday evening), 14 Labour MPs voted against; the legislation passed. Burnham has said he agrees with the "broad thrust" of the plan but faces pressure to modify it to address the party's left.
